title: Green Rule (Safety Gate)
concept: The one rule that can’t be broken: you have to be able to say the honest thing without being punished for it. If that’s not true, everything else stops.
whenToUse: Always — but especially when a topic feels risky to bring up, honesty feels like it’ll cost you, or someone starts threatening, shutting down, or getting back at the other.
steps: Say what feels unsafe, in one sentence.
Stop talking about the topic right away — don’t try to prove your point first.
Take a Pause + Return, with an exact time to come back. If it’s fear, threats, coercion or violence — not just flooding — don’t return at the set time: leave safely and use the Help Lines.
When you’re back, warm up and make sure it’s safe again before you return to the topic.
Repair the safety break with a phrase you’ve both agreed on.

phrases.text: This doesn’t feel safe right now.
Can we pause? This doesn’t feel safe.
Even if I don’t like what you say, I won’t punish you for saying it.

working: A: “I want to be honest about this, but I’m worried you’ll shut down.” B: “Thank you for saying it. I’m getting flooded. Pause 20 minutes — back at 8.10pm. Not leaving; I want to hear it.” A: “See you at 8.10pm.”
notWorking: “Fine, tell me — but if it’s what I think, I don’t know why we’re together.” Now the honest thing gets punished, so next time it won’t get said. Misuse: saying “this doesn’t feel safe” to shut down every complaint. The Green Rule protects honesty; it is not a veto.
activity: Each of you writes one sentence for when something doesn’t feel safe. Agree on your default pause length. Practise with one low-stakes but honest example — the listener just acknowledges it, without arguing back.
warn: The Green Rule comes before every other tool in this system. If you’re afraid of your partner, being threatened, or not free to say no, stop: these tools are not for this. Get outside help.
